name: Zen
comment: DELIBERATELY THREE RULES. Colour is the server's job (textDocument/semanticTokens, out of the compiler's own lexer) and this file must never grow into a second colouriser competing with it. It exists because VS Code decides what is a BRACKET before it has ever spoken to the server, and it decides it from TextMate scopes: with no grammar at all every byte is plain text, so the `(` in out.add_bytes("(zg_fs_kind(") matched as a real bracket. Semantic tokens cannot fix that -- they arrive asynchronously and bracket matching never consults them. So this names only what brackets must be excluded from: comments, strings and character literals. Keywords, numbers, types, functions and parameters are absent on purpose; the server colours those, and it knows what they mean.

char.comment: One regex and not a begin/end pair: an unpaired apostrophe must not open a scope that swallows the rest of the file.
char.name: string.quoted.single.zen
